I withdrew the finding: the spec doesn't contradict itself here.

The cited line (`hw/ip/aon_timer/doc/theory_of_operation.md:25`) says "Register reads via the TL-UL interface (SYS domain) are synchronized to the slow clock". It doesn't say all accesses. The next lines say writes can complete before reaching the slow-clock register, and that a read-back guarantees earlier writes have completed. Those fit together, because the async interface crosses clock domains and a read-back waits for it.

The "reads" wording is loose, since the async feature covers all accesses. Rewording line 25 to "Register accesses" would remove the confusion. I didn't check the RTL, so I can't say which side it matches.
